Introduction

Definition 1 (associativity) For all \(a,b,{c}\) in \(S\), one has \((a \cdot b) \cdot c=a \cdot (b \cdot c)}\).


Definition 2 (identity) There exists an element \(e\) in \(S\) Such that, for every \(a\) in \(S\), one has \(e \cdot a={a}\) and \(a \cdot e={a}\). Such an element is unique and is called the identity element.


Definition 3 (unique inverse) For each \(a\) in \(S\), there exists an element \(b\) in \(S\) Such that \(a \cdot b=e\) and \(b \cdot a=e\), where \(e\) is the identity element.
For each \(a\), the element \(b\) is unique and is called the inverse of \(b\) and is denoted \(a^{-1}\).
